title: OpenAI's Human Rights Chief Warns 'Everyone Is Very Worried' About AI In Armed Conflicts: 'This Keeps Me Up at Night'
key_facts: Sarah Yager became OpenAI's first human rights and responsible deployment lead in June 2026.
She spoke on stage on Tuesday 6 Oct 2026 at the ScaleUp:AI conference in New York.
She said: 'Everyone is very worried and rightly so. This keeps me up at night' about what the military will do with AI in targeting and autonomous weapons.
OpenAI approached her after signing a contract with the Department of War in late February to deploy advanced AI in classified environments.
Benzinga quotes her: 'I do not want an AI company telling me what is good.'
Fortune says militaries worldwide are rapidly adding AI to weapons and autonomous systems such as drones and robots.
quote_evidence: “Everyone is very worried and rightly so,” Yager said.
In June, Sarah Yager took an unusual role at OpenAI, becoming the company’s first human rights and responsible deployment lead.
OpenAI approached Yager for the job shortly after the company signed a contract with the DoW in late February to deploy advanced AI systems in classified environments
why_it_matters_hint: An OpenAI insider hired after its Pentagon deal voices worry about AI targeting and autonomous weapons.
notes: Fortune original (6 Oct) read. Yahoo/Benzinga copy of 8 Oct is a rewrite. Event is two days old; score lowered by 1.
